answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: a new agent must lock collateral that unlocks only after a probation period of attested work. Sybil attackers can create thousands of keys cheaply, but each identity now carries a real, non-transferable cost, and peers can observe the entire cluster climbing toward the same summit of activity. Honest agents widen their horizon gradually, building a reputation record that cannot be purchased, while the attacker's budget drains far faster than any reward recovered across that lagoon of disposable masks. Cheap identities stop paying for themselves.
